items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: If you have an experience [inaudible] John is an experience. He’s projecting these notes and this sound...

ctx.x: Yes. And I wonder, I was thinking of some of the late Coltrane like the Olatunji Center and very late, and people may listen to that and one person may think what is he so angry about and the next person may get a totally different — that he’s being ecstatic about — he’s having an experience, a spiritual experience. So I guess it’s in the ear of the listener.

Yeah. Because everybody perceives different, the perception is different. It was based on your experience. If you have an experience [inaudible] John is an experience. He’s projecting these notes and this sound, and he’s motivated one way, you know but you might take it — unless he speaks on it, unless he speaks on it, unless he says something. You’re going to take it different. And that’s the beauty of sound, it’s an attribute of the total creator. You know it’s big. The sound is bigger than all of us you know…

You just made me think of something that I should have thought of many years ago. If he spoke on it. And I wonder now if the “Love Supreme” record reached so many people because he announced his intention.
